{{Quote|A particularly vicious combatant and one who fought valiantly in three separate Bloodings&hellip;|Lak Sivrak, speaking of Myo in a report to the Alliance High Command|<ref name="AIR" />}}
'''Myo''' was a vicious [[Abyssin/Legends|Abyssin]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] who was a native of the desert [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Byss (Abyssin)/Legends|Byss]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. As a youth, he proved himself to be a fearless warrior, surviving three tribal [[Blooding]]s on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. He lived most of his life in isolation from his fellow Abyssin after being captured by a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Slavery/Legends|slaver]] named [[Malak (Rodian)|Malak]] and taken off-world. Myo was able to escape his captor while her [[Starship/Legends|starship]] was [[Fuel/Legends|refueling]] at [[Kinun Depot]], however, and eventually befriended the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] musician [[Lirin Car'n/Legends|Lirin Car'n]], who provided him with passage to the arid world of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

Myo became a regular patron of [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Cantina]], becoming fast friends with many of his fellow drinkers, including Car'n, [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]], and [[Dorlar]]. Dorlar eventually offered Myo a position working for the [[Galactic Outdoor Survival School/Legends|Galactic Outdoor Survival School]], and the Abyssin served as a desert instructor for at least two years during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Like all Abyssin, Myo possessed amazing regenerative abilities, which aided him greatly when living in barren conditions, as well as in brawls.

==Biography==
===Early life===
Myo was a hulking, cyclopean [[Abyssin/Legends|Abyssin]] from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Byss (Abyssin)/Legends|Byss]].<ref name="AIR" /> Byss was a barren, desert planet, and the various Abyssin tribes fought over the scarce amounts of [[Water/Legends|water]] in skirmishes called [[Blooding]]s. In each Blooding, opposing tribes would fight with each other at an oasis until one tribe had no one left standing; at that point, the victors were awarded the right to consume the water. Casualties were extremely high, so few survived more than a handful of Bloodings in their life.<ref name="GG4">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref> From a young age, Myo proved himself to be a particularly vicious, fearless, and ill-tempered combatant,<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Myo}}</ref> even among his fellow Abyssin, and while still an adolescent, he participated in no less than three separate Bloodings, emerging on the victorious side in each of them.<ref name="AIR" />

Myo loved the deserts of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]],<ref name="CCG" /> so he was angered when a small time [[Slavery/Legends|slaver]] named [[Malak (Rodian)|Malak]] captured him and took him off-world.<ref name="AIR" /> Malak, a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]], specialized in the capture and sale of primitive and exotic [[Species/Legends|species]] and had a penchant for leading violent raids against unsuspecting communities,<ref name="GG11">''[[Galaxy Guide 11: Criminal Organizations]]''</ref> like those on Byss. Longing to return to the desert, Myo eventually escaped Malak's clutches around [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], freeing himself from her ship while it was refueling at [[Kinun Depot]]. He chanced upon a [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] musician named [[Lirin Car'n/Legends|Lirin Car'n]], who acted as a backup [[Kloo horn/Legends|kloo horn]] player in a popular musical act named [[Figrin D'an/Legends|Figrin D'an]] [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|and the Modal Nodes]]. The two became fast friends and when Car'n offered Myo passage to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]<ref name="AIR" />&mdash;a world not unlike his homeworld&mdash;the Abyssin could not pass up the opportunity to return to desert terrain.<ref name="FF" />

===Survival expert===
Myo was able to indulge his violent tendencies again on Tatooine, and he embroiled himself in many fights. His natural regenerative abilities allowed him to shrug off otherwise grievous injuries,<ref name="CCG" /> though they also helped mold him into a desert survival expert.<ref name="FF" /> Myo became a [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]], as well as an associate of Lirin Car'n, and often frequented the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley cantina]] with the Bith; with Myo being something of an [[Alcohol/Legends|alcoholic]], spirits were the fastest way to win the Abyssin's friendship. Myo also befriended a [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] named [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]], another being who frequented the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]].<ref name="AIR" /> In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Myo and Car'n witnessed a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] named [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] attack another of the tavern's patrons, the [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]] [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]], with a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], though the spectacle only held Myo and his fellow drinkers' attention for a moment.<ref name="ANH" />

[[File:GOSS_members.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Myo with other members of the GOSS.]]
Several weeks later, Myo encountered a friendly [[Brubb]] named [[Dorlar]] who served as an instructor in the [[Galactic Outdoor Survival School/Legends|Galactic Outdoor Survival School]]&mdash;GOSS. Myo took a shining to Dorlar, who was more than willing to provide him with a large amount of alcohol and other amenities, and eventually the Brubb offered him a position working as an instructor for GOSS; the organization had lost a desert assistant and had no one to fill his position for the coming term. Knowing that slavers were still looking to recapture him, Myo agreed and accompanied Dorlar to the planet [[Thrantin]]. Myo worked almost exclusively in desert zones, becoming one of GOSS's most trusted staff members after two years in their employ.<ref name="AIR" />

The leader of the Galactic Outdoor Survival School, [[Barosa Warren]], was firmly opposed to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], although Myo, like many other GOSS staff members, cared little for politics and simply followed whatever orders he was given. Lak Sivrak, Myo's old friend from Mos Eisley, was in fact a prominent scout for the Alliance, and he believed that Myo would make a good recruit for the Rebellion if the Abyssin could be kept away from Warren for long enough.<ref name="AIR" />

==Personality and traits==
Myo was known for his violent, primitive nature, and he had a reputation as one of the best combatants on Tatooine. He had a very short temper, and any perceived insults against him were punished promptly and severely; if someone even muttered the term ''[[monoc]]'' in his presence, he would start a fight with them.<ref name="CCG" /> He was even known to take others' lives for poking fun at his eye.<ref name="FF" /> Because of his desert upbringing and his regenerative abilities, Myo was able to survive in barren, waterless areas for a long period of time, eventually becoming a well trained, expert survivalist. However, Myo did have another, friendlier side to him, and he often socialized with other patrons of [[Chalmun/Legends|Chalmun's]] cantina. Myo's personality differed slightly from his fellow Abyssin, as he lived most of his life in isolation from members of his species,<ref name="AIR" /> who had a strong sense of community.<ref name="GG4" />

==Skills and abilities==
Myo utilized headlocks when fighting.<ref name="H2H" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Bts_Myo.jpg|thumb|180px|Myo's mask from ''A New Hope''.]]
An unnamed cyclopean creature appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] in [[1977]], who was initially to be called "Cyceyed" in [[1978]]. That name, however, was lost to time, and the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] established that the character was actually Myo, an Abyssin who debuted in a [[West End Games]] sourcebook titled ''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''. ''Alliance Intelligence Reports'' established Myo's backstory as a mercenary and survival expert. In ''A New Hope'', Myo was portrayed by uncredited creature designer [[Phil Tippett]],<ref name="Aveleyman">{{WebCite|url=http://www.aveleyman.com/ActorCredit.aspx?ActorID=25347|text=Phil Tippett|work=Aveleyman.com|archivedate=20181104144225}}</ref> who was reported to be scrawny in comparison to Myo. Tippett wore a slip-on mask designed by [[Laine Liska]], which had limited mouth and eye articulation.<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> The mask was also used in ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''.<ref name="HS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref>
